title.raw: 卷56 鄭羲 崔辯 Volume 56: Zheng Xi, Cui Bian

sentences.zh: 鄭羲 崔辯

translations.literal: Zheng Xi, Cui Bian
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi and Cui Bian

sentences.zh: 鄭羲，字幼驎，滎陽開封人，魏將作大匠渾之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xi, styled Youlin, was a man of Kaifeng in Xingyang, the eighth-generation descendant of Hun, Director of Palace Construction under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi, courtesy name Youlin, came from Kaifeng in Xingyang. He was the eighth-generation descendant of Hun, who had served as Director of Palace Construction under the state of Wei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖豁，慕容垂太常卿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Huo was Grand Master of Ceremonies under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Huo had been Grand Master of Ceremonies under Murong Chui of Former Yan.

sentences.zh: 父曄，不仕，娶于長樂潘氏，生六子，粗有志氣，而羲第六，文學為優。

translations.literal: His father Ye did not take office; he married the Pan clan of Changle and had six sons. They were roughly spirited, and Xi was the sixth, outstanding in letters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ye never held office. He married into the Pan clan of Changle and fathered six sons, all men of some spirit. Xi was the sixth of them and excelled in literary learning.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，尚書李孝伯以女妻之。

translations.literal: At his capping he was recommended as xiucai; the Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Xiaobo gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was recommended as a xiucai candidate, and Li Xiaobo of the Masters of Writing gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: At the end of the reign of Emperor Gaozong he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天安初，劉彧司州刺史常珍奇據汝南來降，顯祖詔殿中尚書元石為都將赴之，并招慰淮汝，遣羲參石軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an, Liu Yu's Inspector of Sizhou Chang Zhenqi held Runan and came to surrender. Emperor Xianzu ordered Yuan Shi of the Palace Secretariat as supreme commander to go there, and also to win over and comfort the Huai and Ru regions, sending Xi to serve on Shi's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tian'an era, Chang Zhenqi, Liu Yu's inspector of Sizhou, held Runan and defected to the north. Emperor Xianzu appointed Yuan Shi of the Palace Secretariat supreme commander to accept him and to pacify the Huai and Ru regions, and dispatched Xi to serve on Shi's staff.

sentences.zh: 到上蔡，珍奇率文武三百人來迎，既相見，議欲頓軍於汝北，未即入城。

translations.literal: When they reached Shangcai, Zhenqi led three hundred civil and military men to welcome them. After they met, they discussed halting the army north of the Ru and not entering the city at once.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Shangcai, Zhenqi came out with three hundred civil and military officials to welcome them. After the meeting the commanders debated halting the army north of the Ru rather than entering the city immediately.

sentences.zh: 羲謂石曰：「機事尚速，今珍奇雖來，意未可量，不如直入其城，奪其管籥，據有府庫，雖出其非意，要以全制為勝。

translations.literal: Xi said to Shi: "Urgent affairs favor speed. Though Zhenqi has come now, his intentions cannot yet be measured. It would be better to enter his city at once, seize the keys of office, and hold the treasuries. Though this goes against his expectations, complete control is the winning move."
translations.idiomatic: Xi told Shi, "In matters of opportunity, speed is everything. Zhenqi may have come over, but his intentions are still uncertain. Better to ride straight into the city, seize the keys of office, and take the treasuries. It may catch him off guard, but full control is how we win."

sentences.zh: 」石從羲言，遂策馬徑入其城。

translations.literal: Shi followed Xi's words and spurred his horse straight into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shi took his advice and spurred his horse straight through the gates.

sentences.zh: 城中尚有珍奇親兵數百人，在珍奇宅內。

translations.literal: Within the city there were still several hundred of Zhenqi's personal troops in Zhenqi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of Zhenqi's personal troops were still quartered in his residence inside the city.

sentences.zh: 石既克城，意益驕怠，置酒嬉戲，無警防之虞。

translations.literal: Once Shi had taken the city, his mind grew ever more arrogant and slack; he set out wine and amused himself, with no thought of guard or defense.
translations.idiomatic: Once the city was his, Shi grew arrogant and careless. He set out wine and amused himself, giving no thought to security.

sentences.zh: 羲謂石曰：「觀珍奇甚有不平之色，可嚴兵設備，以待非常。

translations.literal: Xi said to Shi: "I observe that Zhenqi shows much resentment. You should tighten the troops and set defenses to await the unexpected."
translations.idiomatic: Xi warned Shi, "Zhenqi looks deeply discontent. You should keep the troops on alert and post guards against any surprise."

sentences.zh: 」其夜，珍奇果使人燒府廂屋，欲因救火作難，以石有備，乃止。

translations.literal: That night Zhenqi indeed sent men to burn the side buildings of the government compound, intending to raise trouble under cover of fighting the fire; because Shi was prepared, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhenqi did send men to set fire to the government outbuildings, hoping to stage a revolt under cover of the blaze. Because Shi was prepared, the plot came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 明旦，羲齎白虎幡慰郭邑，眾心乃定。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Xi carried the white-tiger banner to reassure the outer districts, and the people's hearts were settled.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Xi toured the outer districts bearing the white-tiger banner of reassurance, and the people's minds were calmed.

sentences.zh: 明年春，又引軍東討汝陰。

translations.literal: The next spring he again led the army east to attack Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the army marched east again to attack Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 劉彧汝陰太守張超城守不下，石率精銳攻之，不克，遂退至陳項，議欲還軍長社，待秋擊之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's Administrator of Ruyin Zhang Chao held the city and could not be taken down. Shi led picked troops to attack but could not overcome him, then withdrew to Chenxiang. They discussed returning the army to Changshe and waiting until autumn to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao, Liu Yu's administrator of Ruyin, held the city and could not be dislodged. Shi led elite troops against him but failed, then fell back to Chenxiang. The commanders debated withdrawing to Changshe and waiting until autumn to renew the attack.

sentences.zh: 諸將心樂早還，咸稱善計。

translations.literal: The generals' hearts delighted in an early return, and all praised the plan as good.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were eager to get home and all praised the plan.

sentences.zh: 羲曰：「今張超驅市人，負擔石，[1]蟻聚窮城，命不延月，宜安心守之。

translations.literal: Xi said: "Now Zhang Chao drives market folk who shoulder stones, [1] swarming like ants in a desperate city. His fate will not extend a month. You should settle in and besiege him in peace."
translations.idiomatic: Xi objected: "Zhang Chao has only market folk shouldering stones, [1] packed like ants into a doomed city. He cannot last a month. We should sit tight and wait him out."

sentences.zh: 超食已盡，不降當走，可翹足而待，成擒物也。

translations.literal: When Chao's food is exhausted, if he does not surrender he will flee. You can wait with feet crossed; capture is assured.
translations.idiomatic: When his grain runs out he will either surrender or flee. We can sit with folded legs and take him at leisure—it is a prize already as good as won.

sentences.zh: 而欲棄還長社，道塗懸遠，超必修城深壍，多積薪穀，將來恐難圖矣。

translations.literal: Yet you wish to abandon the siege and return to Changshe. The road is long and remote; Chao is sure to repair the walls and deepen the moats and store much fuel and grain. In the future I fear he will be hard to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If we pull back to Changshe now, the march is long and Chao will surely repair his walls, deepen his moats, and stockpile fuel and grain. When we return he will be far harder to take."

sentences.zh: 」石不納，遂旋師長社。

translations.literal: Shi did not accept this and turned the army back to Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Shi would not listen and marched back to Changshe.

sentences.zh: 至冬，復往攻超，超果設備，無功而還。

translations.literal: By winter they went again to attack Chao. Chao had indeed made preparations, and they returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they attacked Chao again. He had fortified as Xi had predicted, and the expedition came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 歷年，超死，楊文長代戍，食盡城潰，乃克之，竟如羲策。

translations.literal: After years Chao died. Yang Wenchang replaced him on garrison duty. When food was exhausted the city collapsed, and they took it—exactly as Xi's plan had foretold.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Chao died. Yang Wenchang took over the garrison. When supplies ran out the city fell apart and the northerners took it—just as Xi had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 淮北平，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the north of the Huai was pacified, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huai region was pacified he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延興初，陽武人田智度，年十五，妖惑動眾，擾亂京索。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanxing, Tian Zhidu of Yangwu, fifteen years old, used sorcery to stir the masses and disturbed the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanxing era, a fifteen-year-old named Tian Zhidu of Yangwu used sorcery to rouse a following and threw the capital region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 以羲河南民望，為州郡所信，遣羲乘傳慰諭。

translations.literal: Because Xi was the people's hope in Henan and trusted by the provinces and commanderies, they sent Xi by post carriage to comfort and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xi enjoyed the people's trust throughout Henan and was respected by local officials, the court sent him by fast carriage to reassure the populace.

sentences.zh: 羲到，宣示禍福，重加募賞，旬日之間，眾皆歸散。

translations.literal: When Xi arrived he proclaimed fortune and misfortune and added heavy rewards for recruitment. Within ten days the masses all dispersed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi arrived he explained the consequences of rebellion and offered generous rewards for those who stood down. Within ten days the crowd had scattered.

sentences.zh: 智度奔潁川，尋見擒斬。

translations.literal: Zhidu fled to Yingchuan and was soon captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidu fled to Yingchuan and was soon captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵平昌男，加鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the title Baron of Pingchang and given the additional rank of General Who Rouses the Hawks.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was ennobled as Baron of Pingchang and given the additional rank of General Who Rouses the Hawks.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，兼員外散騎常侍，假寧朔將軍、陽武子，使於劉準。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he concurrently served as Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment, with acting rank as General Who Pacifies the North and Viscount of Yangwu, and was sent on mission to Liu Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign he served concurrently as supernumerary Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, with acting rank as General Who Pacifies the North and Viscount of Yangwu, and was sent on embassy to Liu Zhun of the south.

sentences.zh: 中山王叡，[2]寵幸當世，並置王官，羲為其傅。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhongshan Rui [2] was favored in his age and established a full princely staff; Xi served as his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui of Zhongshan [2] was the favorite of his day and maintained a full princely household; Xi became his tutor.

sentences.zh: 是後歷年不轉，資產亦乏，因請假歸，遂磐桓不返。

translations.literal: After this, for years he received no promotion and his assets were also scant. He therefore asked leave to return home and then lingered without coming back.
translations.idiomatic: For years afterward he received no promotion and his means grew thin. He asked leave to return home and then simply stayed away.

sentences.zh: 及李沖貴寵，與羲姻好，乃就家徵為中書令。

translations.literal: When Li Chong came into high favor and was allied to Xi by marriage, they summoned him from his home to be Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong rose to power and favor—he was related to Xi by marriage—the court summoned Xi from his home to serve as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文明太后為父燕宣王立廟於長安，初成，以羲兼太常卿，假滎陽侯，具官屬，詣長安拜廟，刊石建碑於廟門。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming built a temple at Chang'an for her father, Prince Xuan of Yan. When it was first completed, she made Xi concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies, with acting rank as Marquis of Xingyang and a full staff, to go to Chang'an to worship at the temple and carve stone and erect a stele at the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming had built a temple at Chang'an for her father, Prince Xuan of Yan. When it was finished she appointed Xi concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies, with acting rank as Marquis of Xingyang and a full staff, to travel to Chang'an for the dedication and to carve and set up a stele at the gate.

sentences.zh: 還，以使功，仍賜侯爵，加給事中。

translations.literal: On his return, for his mission's merit he was again granted a marquisate and given the additional post of Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: On his return his embassy was rewarded with a permanent marquisate and the additional post of Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 出為安東將軍、西兗州刺史，假南陽公。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Western Yanzhou, with acting rank as Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Western Yanzhou, with acting rank as Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 羲多所受納，政以賄成。

translations.literal: Xi accepted many bribes; his government was accomplished through gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Xi accepted bribes freely and ran his administration through graft.

sentences.zh: 性又嗇吝，民有禮餉者，皆不與杯酒臠肉，西門受羊酒，東門酤賣之。

translations.literal: By nature he was also stingy. When the people brought ceremonial gifts he would not give them even a cup of wine or a slice of meat. At the west gate he received sheep and wine; at the east gate he sold them.
translations.idiomatic: He was miserly as well. When commoners brought him gifts of courtesy he would not offer them so much as a cup of wine or a slice of meat. He accepted sheep and wine at the west gate and sold them out the east.

sentences.zh: 以李沖之親，法官不之糾也。

translations.literal: Because of his kinship with Li Chong, the law officers did not investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his connection to Li Chong, the judicial authorities never called him to account.

sentences.zh: 酸棗令鄭伯孫、鄄城令童騰、別駕賈德、治中申靈度，並在任廉貞，勤恤百姓，羲皆申表稱薦，時論多之。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Suanzao Zheng Bosun, the magistrate of Juancheng Tong Teng, the vice-prefect Jia De, and the chief clerk Shen Lingdu were all upright in office and diligent in caring for the people. Xi submitted memorials recommending them all, and contemporary opinion praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrates Zheng Bosun of Suanzao and Tong Teng of Juancheng, the vice-prefect Jia De, and the chief clerk Shen Lingdu all served with integrity and cared diligently for the people. Xi memorialized recommending each of them, and public opinion commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 文明太后為高祖納其女為嬪，徵為祕書監。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming took his daughter as a consort for Emperor Gaozu, and he was summoned to be Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming took his daughter as a consort for Emperor Gaozu, Xi was recalled to serve as Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 太和十六年卒，贈帛五百匹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Taihe he died. Five hundred bolts of silk were granted in condolence.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Taihe (492). The court granted five hundred bolts of silk for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏諡曰宣，詔曰：「蓋棺定諡，先典成式，激揚清濁，治道明範。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing memorialized that his posthumous title should be Xuan. An edict said: "When the coffin is closed the posthumous name is fixed—this is the established pattern of ancient precedent, to exalt the pure and cast down the foul, a clear model for governing principle."
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing proposed the posthumous name Xuan ("Splendid"). The emperor replied in an edict: "Fixing the posthumous name when the coffin is closed is the established rule of antiquity, meant to exalt the worthy and condemn the base—a clear standard for governance."

sentences.zh: 故何曾幼孝，良史不改『繆醜』之名；

translations.literal: Thus He Zeng showed filial piety in youth, yet good historians did not alter the name 'Miu Chou' (Deceptive and Ugly);
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng was filial from childhood, yet honest historians did not change his name to anything but Miu Chou—"Deceptive and Ugly";

sentences.zh: 賈充寵晉，直士猶立『荒公』之稱。

translations.literal: Jia Chong was favored in Jin, yet upright men still set up for him the title 'Duke Huang' (Reckless).
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong was the favorite of Jin, yet upright scholars still gave him the title Duke Huang—"Reckless."

sentences.zh: 羲雖宿有文業，而治闕廉清。

translations.literal: Though Xi long had literary accomplishment, in governing he lacked integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had long been known for literary accomplishment, but in office he lacked integrity.

sentences.zh: 稽古之効，未光於朝策；

translations.literal: The effect of his study of antiquity did not shine in court policy;
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship never translated into enlightened court policy;

sentences.zh: 昧貨之談，已形於民聽。

translations.literal: talk of coveting goods had already taken shape in what the people heard.
translations.idiomatic: and talk of his greed had already reached the people's ears.

sentences.zh: 諡以善問，殊乖其衷。

translations.literal: To give the posthumous name of a good inquiry is greatly at odds with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: To give him a flattering posthumous name would be wholly contrary to the facts.

sentences.zh: 又前歲之選，匪由備行充舉，自荷後任，勳績未昭。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the selection of the previous year he was not recommended through full qualification and conduct; since he bore later responsibilities, his achievements and merit were not yet clear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his recent appointment was not based on fully qualified merit, and since taking higher office he had shown no distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 尚書何乃情遺至公，愆違明典！

translations.literal: How could the Masters of Writing, in feeling, abandon utmost fairness and violate the clear statutes!
translations.idiomatic: How could the Masters of Writing, out of personal feeling, abandon fairness and violate the clear statutes!

sentences.zh: 依諡法：博聞多見曰『文』，不勤成名曰『靈』。

translations.literal: According to the rules of posthumous naming: broad learning and many observations are called 'Wen'; not striving yet achieving a name is called 'Ling.'
translations.idiomatic: By the rules of posthumous naming: broad learning and wide knowledge warrant Wen—"Cultivated"; achieving a reputation without real effort warrants Ling—"Unworthy."

sentences.zh: 可贈以本官，加諡文靈。」

translations.literal: He may be granted his former office and given the additional posthumous name Wen Ling."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him his former rank and add the posthumous name Wen Ling—"Cultivated yet Unworthy."

sentences.zh: 長子懿，字景伯。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yi, styled Jingbo.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yi, courtesy name Jingbo,

sentences.zh: 涉歷經史，善當世事。

translations.literal: traversed the classics and histories and was skilled in affairs of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: was versed in the classics and histories and adept at the affairs of his day.

sentences.zh: 解褐中散，尚書郎，稍遷驃騎長史、尚書吏部郎、太子中庶子，襲爵滎陽伯。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the russet he served as Palace Attendant, Master of Writing, and was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry, Director of the Personnel Section of the Masters of Writing, and Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, inheriting the title Baron of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Palace Attendant and Master of Writing, then rose through Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry, Director of the Personnel Section, and Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, inheriting the barony of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 懿閑雅有治才，為高祖所器遇，拜長兼給事黃門侍郎、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Yi was refined and elegant and had talent for governing; Emperor Gaozu valued and favored him, appointing him Senior Concurrent Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and capable in administration, Yi won Emperor Gaozu's favor and was appointed Senior Concurrent Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Chief Clerk of the Left under the Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，以從弟思和同咸陽王禧之逆，與弟通直常侍道昭俱坐緦親出禁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, because his cousin Sikong was implicated in the rebellion of Prince Xianyang Xi, he and his younger brother the Direct Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Daozhao were both punished as distant kin and expelled from office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign, because his cousin Sikong was implicated in Prince Xi's rebellion, Yi and his younger brother Daozhao, Direct Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, were both punished as distant kin and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 拜太常少卿，加冠軍將軍，出為征虜將軍、齊州刺史，尋進號平東將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, given the additional rank of Champion General, and sent out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Qizhou; soon his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Vice Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies with the additional rank of Champion General, then sent out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and inspector of Qizhou, soon promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 懿好勸課，善斷決，雖不潔清，義然後取，百姓猶思之。

translations.literal: Yi loved to encourage agriculture and was skilled in judgments. Though not pure and clean, he took only when it was justified, and the people still remembered him fondly.
translations.idiomatic: Yi encouraged agriculture and judged cases well. Though not spotlessly honest, he took only what he could justify, and the people still remembered him with affection.

sentences.zh: 永平三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Yongping (510).

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、兗州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former general's rank and the post of Inspector of Yanzhou; his posthumous name was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former general's rank and the post of inspector of Yanzhou, with the posthumous name Mu—"Solemn."

sentences.zh: 子恭業，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Gongye inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongye inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定三年，坐與房子遠謀逆，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuding he was punished for plotting rebellion with Fang Ziyuan and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuding (545) he was executed for plotting rebellion with Fang Ziyuan.

sentences.zh: 懿弟道昭，字僖伯。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Daozhao, styled Xibo.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Daozhao, courtesy name Xibo,

sentences.zh: 少而好學，綜覽羣言。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and surveyed all the schools of discourse.
translations.idiomatic: loved learning from youth and read widely across the schools of thought.

sentences.zh: 初為中書學生，遷祕書郎，拜主文中散，徙員外散騎侍郎、祕書丞、兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He first served as a student of the Secretariat, was transferred to Secretary of the Palace Library, appointed Chief Palace Attendant for Drafting, and moved to Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment, Secretary of the Palace Library, and Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a student of the Secretariat, then served as Secretary of the Palace Library, Chief Palace Attendant for Drafting, Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment, Secretary of the Palace Library, and Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從征沔漢，高祖饗侍臣於懸瓠方丈竹堂，道昭與兄懿俱侍坐焉。

translations.literal: On the campaign against the Mian and Han regions, Emperor Gaozu feasted his attending ministers in the square-zhanger bamboo hall at Xuanhuo; Daozhao and his elder brother Yi both attended seated there.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against the Mian and Han regions, Emperor Gaozu feasted his ministers in the square-zhanger bamboo hall at Xuanhuo. Daozhao and his brother Yi were both in attendance.

sentences.zh: 樂作酒酣，高祖乃歌曰：「白日光天無不曜，江左一隅獨未照。

translations.literal: When the music played and the wine was deep, Emperor Gaozu sang: "The white sun shines on heaven—nothing is not illumined; only one corner of the lands south of the Yangtze is not yet lit."
translations.idiomatic: As the music played and the wine flowed, Emperor Gaozu sang: "The white sun fills the sky and leaves nothing unlit—yet one corner south of the Yangtze still lies in shadow."

sentences.zh: 」彭城王勰續歌曰：「願從聖明兮登衡會，萬國馳誠混江外。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie continued the song: "I wish to follow the sage brilliance and ascend to the balance-meeting; ten thousand states rush their sincerity to blend beyond the river."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Pengcheng took up the verse: "May we follow the sage brilliance to the great assembly, and all lands beyond the river rush to join in loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」鄭懿歌曰：「雲雷大振兮天門闢，率土來賓一正歷。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi sang: "Cloud and thunder greatly shake—the heavenly gate opens; all within the lands come as guests to one correct calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi sang: "Cloud and thunder shake the heavens—the celestial gate opens wide; all within the realm come as guests to one true calendar."

sentences.zh: 」邢巒歌曰：「舜舞干戚兮天下歸，文德遠被莫不思。

translations.literal: Xing Luan sang: "Shun danced with shield and axe—the realm returned; civil virtue spread far—none did not think on it."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan sang: "Shun danced with shield and axe and the realm submitted; civil virtue spreads afar and none fail to ponder it."

sentences.zh: 」道昭歌曰：「皇風一鼓兮九地匝，戴日依天清六合。

translations.literal: Daozhao sang: "The imperial wind beats once—the nine regions are encircled; bearing the sun, leaning on heaven, the six harmonies are cleared."
translations.idiomatic: Daozhao sang: "One beat of the imperial wind circles the nine regions; bearing the sun and leaning on heaven, the six directions are made clear."

sentences.zh: 」高祖又歌曰：「遵彼汝墳兮昔化貞，未若今日道風明。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sang again: "Following that bank of the Ru—of old the transformation was true; it is not like today when the Way's wind is bright."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sang again: "Along the banks of the Ru the ancients taught steadfast virtue—yet nothing matches the brightness of the Way's wind today."

sentences.zh: 」宋弁歌曰：「文王政教兮暉江沼，寧如大化光四表。

translations.literal: Song Bian sang: "King Wen's government and teaching shine on the river marshes; how can they compare to the great transformation that lights the four quarters?"
translations.idiomatic: Song Bian sang: "King Wen's governance shone on the river marshes—how can it compare to the great transformation that illuminates the four quarters?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖謂道昭曰：「自比遷務雖猥，與諸才儁不廢詠綴，遂命邢巒總集敍記。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to Daozhao: "Since the move of the capital my duties have been numerous, yet with all you talented men I have not ceased composing verse. I therefore ordered Xing Luan to gather and arrange a record."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told Daozhao, "Since moving the capital my duties have been overwhelming, yet with you talented men I have never stopped composing verse. I have ordered Xing Luan to compile a record of it all."

sentences.zh: 當爾之年，卿頻丁艱禍，每眷文席，常用慨然。

translations.literal: In those years you repeatedly suffered the misfortune of mourning. Whenever I thought of the literary gathering I was often moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: In those years you suffered repeated bereavements. Whenever I thought of our literary gatherings I was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 」尋正除中書郎，轉通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was regularly appointed Master of Writing of the Secretariat and transferred to Direct Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed full Master of Writing of the Secretariat, then transferred to Direct Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 北海王詳為司徒，以道昭與琅邪王秉為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Beihai Xiang served as Minister of State and made Daozhao and Prince of Langye Bing his advisory staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiang of Beihai became Minister of State, he appointed Daozhao and Prince Bing of Langye as his advisory staff officers.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒，道昭表曰：「臣竊以為：崇治之道，必也須才；

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of the National University. Daozhao memorialized: "Your servant ventures to think: the way to exalt governance necessarily requires talent;"
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chancellor of the National University. Daozhao memorialized: "Your servant ventures to believe that the path to exalted governance necessarily requires talent;"

sentences.zh: 養才之要，莫先於學。

translations.literal: the essential of nurturing talent is nothing before learning.
translations.idiomatic: and the essential of nurturing talent is nothing before learning.

sentences.zh: 今國子學堂房粗置，弦誦闕爾。

translations.literal: Now the halls and rooms of the National University are roughly set up, but the plucking and recitation are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Today the halls of the National University are only roughly in place, and the sound of study has fallen silent.

sentences.zh: 城南太學，漢魏石經，丘墟殘毀，藜藋蕪穢，遊兒牧豎，為之歎息，有情之輩，實亦悼心，況臣親司，而不言露。

translations.literal: The Imperial University south of the city—the stone classics of Han and Wei—lie in ruins and wreckage, overgrown with brambles and weeds. Wandering boys and herding lads sigh over them; men of feeling truly grieve in heart. How much more should your servant, who personally oversees this, not speak and reveal it?
translations.idiomatic: South of the city the Imperial University and the Han and Wei stone classics lie in ruins, choked with weeds. Even wandering boys and herdboys sigh at the sight; men of feeling are heartsick. How much more should your servant, who holds this office, fail to speak?

sentences.zh: 伏願天慈回神紆盻，賜垂鑒察。

translations.literal: I bow and wish that Heaven's compassion may turn its spirit and bend its gaze, granting your downward inspection.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will turn a gracious eye and grant your inspection.

sentences.zh: 若臣微意，萬一合允，求重敕尚書、門下，考論營制之模，則五雍可翹立而興，毀銘可不日而就。

translations.literal: If your servant's slight thought should in the least accord with approval, I ask that you again command the Masters of Writing and the Chancellery to examine and discuss models for construction and regulation. Then the Five Yong could be raised standing at once, and ruined inscriptions could be completed within days.
translations.idiomatic: If my humble proposal should meet with approval, I ask that Your Majesty again command the Masters of Writing and the Chancellery to plan the models for reconstruction. Then the Five Yong could rise again at once, and the ruined steles could be restored within days.

sentences.zh: 樹舊經於帝京，播茂範於不朽。

translations.literal: Plant the old classics in the imperial capital and spread flourishing models into immortality.
translations.idiomatic: To plant the ancient classics in the imperial capital and spread a lasting model of excellence—

sentences.zh: 斯有天下者之美業也。

translations.literal: This is the beautiful enterprise of one who possesses the realm.
translations.idiomatic: this is the supreme achievement of one who holds the realm.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: The proposal was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not adopt his proposal.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷為司州牧，以道昭與宗正卿元匡為州都。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangping Huai served as Governor of Sizhou and made Daozhao and the Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Kuang regional commanders of the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Huai of Guangping became governor of Sizhou, he appointed Daozhao and Yuan Kuang, Director of the Imperial Clan, as his provincial staff commanders.

sentences.zh: 道昭又表曰：「臣聞唐虞啟運，以文德為本；

translations.literal: Daozhao again memorialized: "Your servant has heard that when Tang and Yu opened their fortunes, they took civil virtue as the foundation;"
translations.idiomatic: Daozhao memorialized again: "Your servant has heard that when Tang and Yu inaugurated their rule, they took civil virtue as their foundation;"

sentences.zh: 殷周致治，以道藝為先。

translations.literal: Yin and Zhou achieved good government by putting the Way and the arts first.
translations.idiomatic: and that Yin and Zhou achieved good government by putting the Way and the arts first.

sentences.zh: 然則，禮樂者為國之基，不可斯須廢也。

translations.literal: Thus rites and music are the foundation of the state and cannot be abandoned even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus rites and music are the foundation of the state and cannot be abandoned even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 是故周敷文教，四海宅心；

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou spread civil teaching and the four seas made their hearts their home;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou spread civil teaching, the four seas gave their hearts to the throne;

sentences.zh: 魯秉周禮，強齊歸義。

translations.literal: Lu upheld the rites of Zhou and mighty Qi returned to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: when Lu upheld the Zhou rites, even mighty Qi submitted in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 及至戰國紛紜，干戈遞用，五籍灰焚，羣儒坑殄，賊仁義之經，貴戰爭之術，遂使天下分崩，黔黎荼炭，數十年間，民無聊生者，斯之由矣。

translations.literal: When it came to the Warring States in turmoil, weapons and armor were used in succession, the Five Classics were burned to ash, and the mass of scholars were buried alive. They treated the classics of benevolence and righteousness as enemies and prized the arts of war. Thus the realm split apart and the black-haired people suffered bitter coal; for several decades the people had no means of living—this was the cause.
translations.idiomatic: But when the Warring States erupted in chaos, arms followed arms in succession. The Five Classics were burned to ash and the scholars were buried alive. Men treated the scriptures of benevolence and righteousness as enemies and prized the arts of war. The realm split apart and the common people suffered bitterly; for decades the people had no way to live—and this was why.

sentences.zh: 爰暨漢祖，於行陳之中，尚優引叔孫通等。

translations.literal: Down to Han's founder, even amid marching formations he still favored and drew in Shu Sun Tong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Even Han's founder, amid the marching columns of war, still favored and drew in Shu Sun Tong and others.

sentences.zh: 光武中興於撥亂之際，乃使鄭眾、范升校書東觀。

translations.literal: Guangwu in his restoration at the time of quelling disorder then had Zheng Zhong and Fan Sheng collate books at the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu, restoring order amid chaos, had Zheng Zhong and Fan Sheng collate books at the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 降逮魏晉，何嘗不殷勤於篇籍，篤學於戎伍。

translations.literal: Descending to Wei and Jin, when did they not diligently attend to written works and earnestly study even in the military camps?
translations.idiomatic: Down through Wei and Jin, which ruler did not diligently cherish the written heritage and study earnestly even in the military camps?

sentences.zh: 伏惟大魏之興也，雖羣凶未殄，戎馬在郊，然猶招集英儒，廣開學校，用能闡道義於八荒，布盛德於萬國，教靡不懷，風無不偃。

translations.literal: I bow and consider the rise of Great Wei: though many villains were not yet destroyed and war-horses were at the suburbs, yet they still gathered eminent scholars, broadly opened schools, and thereby were able to expound the Way and righteousness through the eight wilds, spread flourishing virtue through ten thousand states—none whom teaching did not embrace, no wind that did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider the rise of Great Wei: though many enemies were not yet destroyed and war-horses stood at the suburbs, the court still gathered eminent scholars and broadly opened schools, and thereby was able to spread the Way and righteousness through the eight directions, broadcast flourishing virtue to all lands—none whom teaching did not win over, no region where the transforming wind did not bend.

sentences.zh: 今者乘休平之基，開無疆之祚，定鼎伊瀍，惟新寶曆，九服感至德之和，四垠懷擊壤之慶。

translations.literal: Now, riding on the foundation of rest and peace, opening boundless fortune, fixing the tripod at Yi and Luo, renewing the precious calendar, the nine domains feel the harmony of utmost virtue, and the four borders cherish the joy of striking the soil.
translations.idiomatic: Today, building on an era of peace and opening boundless fortune, the dynasty has fixed the capital at Yi and Luo and renewed the sacred calendar. The nine domains feel the harmony of supreme virtue, and the four quarters share the joy of a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 而蠢爾閩吳，阻化江湫，先帝爰震武怒，戎車不息。

translations.literal: Yet foolish Min and Wu block transformation at the river's edge; the late emperor then shook martial wrath, and war-chariots did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet foolish Min and Wu still resist civilization at the river's edge. The late emperor roused martial wrath, and the war-chariots have not ceased.

sentences.zh: 而停鑾佇蹕，留心典墳，命故御史中尉臣李彪與吏部尚書、任城王澄等妙選英儒，以崇文教。

translations.literal: Yet he halted the imperial carriage and paused in progress, keeping his heart on the canonical tomes. He ordered the former Censor-in-Chief Li Biao and the Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and others to finely select eminent scholars to exalt civil teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he halted the imperial progress and turned his heart to the classics, ordering the former Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, the Minister of the Masters of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng, and others to select eminent scholars and elevate civil learning.

sentences.zh: 澄等依旨，置四門博士四十人，其國子博士、太學博士及國子助教，宿已簡置。

translations.literal: Cheng and others followed the edict and established forty Erudites of the Four Gates; the National University Erudites, Imperial University Erudites, and National University Assistants had long since been selected and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and his colleagues obeyed and appointed forty Erudites of the Four Gates; the National University erudites, Imperial University erudites, and assistants had already been chosen.

sentences.zh: 伏尋先旨，意在速就，但軍國多事，未遑營立。

translations.literal: I bow and search the former intent: the aim was swift completion, but military and state affairs were many, and there was no leisure to build and establish.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that the original intent was swift completion, but military and state affairs left no leisure to build.

sentences.zh: 自爾迄今，垂將一紀，學官凋落，四術寢廢。

translations.literal: From then until now, nearly a full twelve-year cycle has passed; the learning offices have withered, and the four arts lie dormant and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now nearly twelve years have passed. The schools have decayed and the four arts lie abandoned.

sentences.zh: 遂使碩儒耆德，卷經而不談；

translations.literal: Thus great scholars and venerable worthies roll up their classics and do not discuss them;
translations.idiomatic: Great scholars and venerable elders now roll up their classics and fall silent;

sentences.zh: 俗學後生，遺本而逐末。

translations.literal: vulgar learners and later students abandon the root and pursue the branch.
translations.idiomatic: while vulgar students abandon the root and chase the branch.

sentences.zh: 進競之風，實由於此矣。

translations.literal: The wind of scrambling for advancement truly arises from this.
translations.idiomatic: The fever of scrambling for advancement truly stems from this.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下欽明文思，玄鑒洞遠。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty reveres bright culture and reflection, with profound insight penetrating far.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reveres bright culture and reflection, with insight penetrating to the farthest reaches.

sentences.zh: 越會未款，務修道以來之；

translations.literal: Yue and Kuai have not yet submitted in good faith; you devote yourself to cultivating the Way to draw them in;
translations.idiomatic: Though Yue and Kuai have not yet submitted in good faith, you devote yourself to cultivating the Way to draw them in;

sentences.zh: 遐方後服，敷文教而懷之。

translations.literal: distant regions and late submitters—you spread civil teaching and cherish them.
translations.idiomatic: for distant lands and late submitters you spread civil teaching and win their hearts.

sentences.zh: 垂心經素，優柔墳籍。

translations.literal: You bend your heart to the classics in plain dress and treat the canonical tomes with gentle care.
translations.idiomatic: You bend your heart to the classics and treat the canonical texts with gentle devotion.

sentences.zh: 將使化越軒唐，德隆虞夏。

translations.literal: You will make transformation surpass Xuanyuan and Tang, and virtue tower above Yu and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: You will make civilization surpass the age of Xuanyuan and Tang and virtue tower above Yu and Xia.

sentences.zh: 是故屢發中旨，敦營學館，房宇既修，生徒未立。

translations.literal: Therefore you have repeatedly issued central edicts, earnestly building school halls. The buildings are already repaired, but the students are not yet established.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore you have repeatedly issued edicts earnestly building the schools. The halls are repaired, yet the students are not yet enrolled.

sentences.zh: 臣學陋全經，識蔽篆素，然往年刪定律令，謬預議筵。

translations.literal: Your servant's learning is shallow and does not comprehend the full classics; my understanding is obscured regarding seal script and plain script. Yet in former years, in revising and fixing laws and statutes, I was wrongly admitted to the deliberation mat.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's learning is shallow and my understanding of the classics incomplete. Yet in former years, when laws and statutes were revised, I was admitted to the deliberation council.

sentences.zh: 謹依準前修，尋訪舊事，參定學令，事訖封呈。

translations.literal: I respectfully followed the former regulations, sought out old precedents, and helped fix the school statutes. When the work was finished I sealed and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: I followed the former regulations, sought out old precedents, and helped draft the school statutes, which I sealed and presented when finished.

sentences.zh: 自爾迄今，未蒙報判。

translations.literal: From then until now I have not received a reply or decision.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now I have received no reply.

sentences.zh: 但廢學歷年，經術淹滯。

translations.literal: Yet learning has been abandoned for years, and classical studies stagnate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet learning has been abandoned for years and classical studies stagnate.

sentences.zh: 請學令并制，早敕施行，使選授有依，生徒可準。

translations.literal: I ask that the school statutes and regulations be commanded for early promulgation and implementation, so that selection and appointment have a basis and students have a standard.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the school statutes and regulations be commanded for early promulgation, so that appointments have a basis and students a standard.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「具卿崇儒敦學之意，良不可言。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Your full intent to exalt Confucianism and encourage learning truly cannot be put into words.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Your intent to exalt Confucianism and encourage learning truly cannot be expressed in words.

sentences.zh: 新令尋班，施行無遠，可謂職思其憂，無曠官矣。」

translations.literal: The new statutes will soon be promulgated; their implementation will not be distant. This may be called attending to one's duties with care for their anxieties, with no neglect of office."
translations.idiomatic: The new statutes will soon be promulgated and put into effect without delay. This is truly attending to one's duties with care—no neglect of office."

sentences.zh: 道昭又表曰：「竊惟鼎遷中縣，年將一紀，縉紳褫業，俎豆闕聞，遂使濟濟明朝，無觀風之美，非所以光國宣風，納民軌義。

translations.literal: Daozhao again memorialized: "Your servant ventures to consider: since the tripod moved to the central counties, nearly a twelve-year cycle has passed. Girdled sashes have lost their occupations; sacrificial vessels lack their fragrance. Thus the abundant morning court has no beauty of observing the winds—this is not the way to glorify the state, proclaim the transforming influence, and bring the people into the tracks of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhao memorialized again: "Your servant ventures to consider: since the capital moved to the central region, nearly twelve years have passed. The gentry have lost their occupations and ritual has fallen silent. The abundant morning court lacks the beauty of observing the people's customs—this is not how to glorify the state, spread transforming influence, and bring the people into the paths of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 臣自往年以來，頻請學令，並置生員，前後累上，未蒙一報，故當以臣識淺濫官，無能有所感悟者也。

translations.literal: Your servant, from former years until now, has repeatedly requested school statutes and the establishment of student quotas, submitting memorials before and after, yet has not received a single reply. Thus it must be that your servant's knowledge is shallow, his office undeserved, and he is incapable of inspiring any awakening.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has repeatedly requested school statutes and the enrollment of students, submitting memorial after memorial without a single reply. Perhaps my knowledge is shallow, my office undeserved, and I am incapable of inspiring any response.

sentences.zh: 館宇既修，生房粗構，博士見員，足可講習。

translations.literal: The halls are already repaired, student quarters roughly built, and the erudites currently on staff are sufficient for lecturing and study.
translations.idiomatic: The halls are repaired, student quarters roughly built, and the erudites on staff are sufficient for instruction.

sentences.zh: 雖新令未班，請依舊權置國子學生，漸開訓業，使播教有章，儒風不墜，後生覩徙義之機，學徒崇知新之益。

translations.literal: Though the new statutes are not yet promulgated, I ask that by the old authority National University students be provisionally appointed, gradually opening instruction, so that spreading teaching has order, Confucian wind does not fall, later students see the occasion for moving toward righteousness, and learners honor the benefit of knowing the new.
translations.idiomatic: Though the new statutes are not yet promulgated, I ask that National University students be provisionally enrolled by former authority, gradually opening instruction so that teaching has order, Confucian learning does not fall, later students see the path toward righteousness, and learners honor the benefit of new knowledge.

sentences.zh: 至若孔廟既成，釋奠告始，揖讓之容，請俟令出。

translations.literal: As for the Confucian temple now completed and the libation sacrifice about to begin, the bearing of bowing and yielding—please wait until the statutes are issued.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Confucian temple now completed and the libation sacrifice about to begin, the ceremonial forms of bowing and yielding should wait until the statutes are issued.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書監、滎陽邑中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Library and Rectifier of Xingyang district.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Library and Rectifier of Xingyang district.

sentences.zh: 出為平東將軍、光州刺史，轉青州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Guangzhou, was transferred to Inspector of Qingzhou, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Guangzhou, then transferred to inspector of Qingzhou, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 復入為祕書監，加平南將軍。

translations.literal: He returned to serve again as Director of the Palace Library, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as Director of the Palace Library with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年卒，贈鎮北將軍、相州刺史，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xiping. He was posthumously granted General Who Guards the North and the post of Inspector of Xiangzhou; his posthumous name was Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Xiping (516). He was posthumously granted General Who Guards the North and the post of inspector of Xiangzhou, with the posthumous name Wengong—"Cultivated and Reverent."

sentences.zh: 道昭好為詩賦，凡數十篇。

translations.literal: Daozhao loved to compose poetry and fu; in all there were several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhao loved to compose poetry and fu; he left several dozen pieces.

sentences.zh: 其在二州，政務寬厚，不任威刑，為吏民所愛。

translations.literal: In the two provinces his government was generous and thick; he did not rely on harsh punishments, and officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: In both provinces his administration was generous and mild; he did not rely on harsh punishments, and officials and commoners loved him.

sentences.zh: 子嚴祖，頗有風儀，粗觀文史。

translations.literal: His son Yanzu had considerable bearing and manner, and a rough acquaintance with letters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanzu had considerable bearing and a rough acquaintance with letters and histories.

sentences.zh: 歷通直郎、通直常侍。

translations.literal: He served as Direct Attendant and Direct Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Direct Attendant and Direct Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 輕躁薄行，不修士業，傾側勢家，乾沒榮利，閨門穢亂，聲滿天下。

translations.literal: He was frivolous and rash, his conduct shallow; he did not cultivate the scholar's calling, leaned toward powerful families, and seized profit by crooked means. His inner quarters were foul and disorderly, and his reputation filled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He was frivolous and rash, neglecting the scholar's calling, currying favor with powerful families and seizing profit by crooked means. His household was foul and disorderly, and his reputation filled the realm.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，御史中尉綦儁劾嚴祖與宗氏從姊姦通。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Chu, the Censor-in-Chief Qi Jun impeached Yanzu for adultery with a paternal cousin of the Zong clan.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Chu, Censor-in-Chief Qi Jun impeached Yanzu for adultery with a paternal cousin of the Zong clan.

sentences.zh: 人士咸耻言之，而嚴祖聊無愧色。

translations.literal: Men of standing all felt shame to speak of it, yet Yanzu showed hardly any color of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Men of standing were ashamed to speak of it, yet Yanzu showed hardly a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，除驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign he was appointed General of Rapid Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was appointed General of Rapid Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 出為北豫州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Northern Yuzhou, retaining his former general's rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of Northern Yuzhou, retaining his former general's rank.

sentences.zh: 罷州還，除鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: When he left the province and returned, he was appointed Director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: When he left his province and returned, he was appointed Director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈都督豫兗潁三州諸軍事、□□將軍、司空公、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted command over all military affairs of the three provinces of Yu, Yan, and Ying, [missing characters] General, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted command over military affairs of Yu, Yan, and Ying provinces, the rank of [missing] General, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚴祖弟敬祖，性亦粗疏。

translations.literal: Yanzu's younger brother Jingzu was also coarse and careless by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzu's younger brother Jingzu was also coarse and careless by nature.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 鄭儼之敗也，為鄉人所害。

translations.literal: When Zheng Yan was defeated, he was killed by men of his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yan was defeated, he was killed by men of his home district.

sentences.zh: 敬祖弟述祖，武定中，尚書。

translations.literal: Jingzu's younger brother Shuzu, in the Wuding era, served as Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu's younger brother Shuzu served as Master of Writing during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 述祖弟遵祖，祕書郎。

translations.literal: Shuzu's younger brother Zunzu was Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu's younger brother Zunzu was Secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Assists the State and the post of Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Assists the State and the post of inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遵祖弟順，[3]卒於太常丞。

translations.literal: Zunzu's younger brother Shun [3] died while serving as Assistant Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Zunzu's younger brother Shun [3] died while serving as Assistant Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 自靈太后預政，淫風稍行，及元叉擅權，公為姦穢。

translations.literal: From the time Empress Dowager Ling participated in government, licentious ways gradually spread. When Yuan Cha monopolized power, public conduct became foul and corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Empress Dowager Ling took part in government, licentious ways gradually spread. When Yuan Cha monopolized power, public conduct became foul and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 自此素族名家，遂多亂雜，法官不加糾治，婚宦無貶於世，有識咸以歎息矣。

translations.literal: From this the plain-clan famous families became much disordered and mixed. Law officers did not investigate and correct; marriage and office carried no stigma in the world. Men of insight all sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: From this the great families of good standing fell into disorder. Law officers did not investigate, and marriage and office carried no stigma in the world. Men of insight all sighed over it.

sentences.zh: 羲五兄：長白驎，次小白，次洞林，次叔夜，次連山。

translations.literal: Xi's five elder brothers: the eldest Bailin, next Xiaobai, next Donglin, next Shuye, next Lianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had five elder brothers: the eldest Bailin, then Xiaobai, Donglin, Shuye, and Lianshan.

sentences.zh: 並恃豪門，多行無禮，鄉黨之內，疾之若讎。

translations.literal: All relied on their powerful house and often acted without propriety. Within their home districts they were hated like enemies.
translations.idiomatic: All relied on their powerful house and often acted without propriety. Within their home districts they were hated like enemies.

sentences.zh: 白驎孫道慓，隨郡太守。

translations.literal: Bailin's grandson Daosao was Administrator of Suijun.
translations.idiomatic: Bailin's grandson Daosao was administrator of Suijun.

sentences.zh: 小白，中書博士。

translations.literal: Xiaobai was Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobai was Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子胤伯，有當世器幹。

translations.literal: His son Yinbo had talent and capacity for the present age.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yinbo had talent and capacity fit for his age.

sentences.zh: 自中書博士遷侍郎，轉司空長史。

translations.literal: From Erudite of the Secretariat he was transferred to Attendant, then moved to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: From Erudite of the Secretariat he was promoted to Attendant, then Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 高祖納其女為嬪。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu took his daughter as a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu took his daughter as a consort.

sentences.zh: 出為建威將軍、東徐州刺史，轉廣陵王征東府長史，帶齊郡內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, was transferred to Chief Clerk of Prince of Guangling's Eastern Campaign Headquarters, concurrently serving as Internal Administrator of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Might and inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, then transferred to Chief Clerk of Prince of Guangling's Eastern Campaign Headquarters, concurrently serving as Internal Administrator of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒於鴻臚少卿，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies; his posthumous name was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies, with the posthumous name Jian—"Simple."

sentences.zh: 子希儁，未官而亡。

translations.literal: His son Xijun died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xijun died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 子道育，武定中，開封太守。

translations.literal: His son Daoyu, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoyu was administrator of Kaifeng during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 希儁弟幼儒，好學修謹，時望甚優。

translations.literal: Xijun's younger brother Youru loved learning and was cultivated and careful; his contemporary reputation was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Xijun's younger brother Youru loved learning and was cultivated and careful; his contemporary reputation was excellent.

sentences.zh: 丞相、高陽王雍以女妻之。

translations.literal: The Chancellor, Prince Yong of Gaoyang, gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor, Prince Yong of Gaoyang, gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書郎、通直郎、司州別駕，有當官之稱。

translations.literal: He served as Master of Writing, Direct Attendant, and Vice-Prefect of Sizhou, and had the reputation of fulfilling his office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Master of Writing, Direct Attendant, and Vice-Prefect of Sizhou, earning a reputation for fulfilling his duties.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈散騎常侍、安東將軍、兗州刺史，諡景。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Yanzhou; his posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and inspector of Yanzhou, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 幼儒亡後，妻淫蕩兇悖，肆行無禮。

translations.literal: After Youru's death his wife was licentious, violent, and rebellious, wantonly acting without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: After Youru's death his wife was licentious, violent, and rebellious, wantonly acting without propriety.

sentences.zh: 子敬道、敬德，並亦不才，俱走於關右。

translations.literal: His sons Jingdao and Jingde were both also without talent and both fled to the lands west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jingdao and Jingde were both without talent and fled to the lands west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 幼儒從兄伯猷每謂所親曰：「從弟人才，足為令德，不幸得如此婦，今死復重死，可為悲嘆。」

translations.literal: Youru's cousin Boyou often said to those close to him: "My cousin's talent was sufficient for fine virtue. Unfortunate to have gotten such a wife—now dead yet doubly dead; it is cause for grief and sighing."
translations.idiomatic: Youru's cousin Boyou often said to those close to him: "My cousin's talent was sufficient for fine virtue. Unfortunate to have gotten such a wife—now dead yet doubly dead. It is cause for grief."

sentences.zh: 胤伯弟平城，太尉諮議。

translations.literal: Yinbo's younger brother Pingcheng was Advisory Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yinbo's younger brother Pingcheng was Advisory Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王羽納其女為妃。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangling Yu took his daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Guangling took his daughter as consort.

sentences.zh: 出為東平原太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Eastern Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as administrator of Eastern Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 性清狂使酒，為政貪殘。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure but wild and given to drink; in government he was greedy and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was unrestrained and given to drink; in government he was greedy and cruel.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians and inspector of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 長子伯猷，博學有文才，早知名。

translations.literal: His eldest son Boyou was broadly learned and had literary talent, becoming famous early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Boyou was broadly learned and talented in letters, becoming famous early.

sentences.zh: 舉司州秀才，以射策高第，除幽州平北府外兵參軍，轉太學博士，領殿中御史。

translations.literal: He was recommended as xiucai of Sizhou and, through archery-and-policy examination with high rank, was appointed Outside Army Staff Officer of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters of Youzhou, transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University, and concurrently served as Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as xiucai of Sizhou and, through the policy examination with high rank, was appointed Outside Army Staff Officer of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters of Youzhou, then Erudite of the Imperial University and concurrent Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 與當時名勝，咸申遊款。

translations.literal: With the famous worthies of the time he all extended friendly visits.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated friendly relations with all the famous worthies of his day.

sentences.zh: 肅宗釋奠，詔伯猷錄義。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong performed the libation sacrifice, he ordered Boyou to record the meanings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong performed the libation sacrifice, he ordered Boyou to record the ritual meanings.

sentences.zh: 安豐王延明之征徐州也，引為行臺郎中。

translations.literal: When Prince of Anfeng Yanming campaigned against Xuzhou, he recruited him as Bureau Director of the Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yanming of Anfeng campaigned against Xuzhou, he recruited Boyou as Bureau Director of the Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 事寧還都，遷尚書外兵郎中，典起居注，以軍功賜爵陽武子。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he returned to the capital, was transferred to Outside Army Bureau Director of the Masters of Writing, supervised the Imperial Diary, and for military merit was granted the title Viscount of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he returned to the capital, was transferred to Outside Army Bureau Director of the Masters of Writing, supervised the Imperial Diary, and for military merit was ennobled as Viscount of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 稍遷散騎常侍、平東將軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，以舅氏超授征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Former Emperor's reign, because of his maternal uncle's connection he was exceptionally granted General Who Campaigns East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, and concurrent Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Deposed Former Emperor's reign, through his maternal uncle's connection he was exceptionally granted General Who Campaigns East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, and concurrent Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 久之，為車騎將軍、右光祿大夫，轉護軍將軍。

translations.literal: After a long time he served as General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then was transferred to General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he served as General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then was transferred to General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 元象初，以本官兼散騎常侍使於蕭衍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he served in his former office concurrently as Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary on embassy to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanxiang era he served concurrently as Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary on embassy to Xiao Yan of Liang.

sentences.zh: 前後使人，蕭衍令其侯王於馬射之日宴對申禮。

translations.literal: Envoys before and after: Xiao Yan had his marquises and princes receive them at banquets on horse-archery days with full courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Previous envoys had been received by Xiao Yan's marquises and princes at banquets on horse-archery days with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 伯猷之行，衍令其領軍將軍臧盾與之相接。

translations.literal: On Boyou's mission, Yan had his Army Commander Zang Dun receive him.
translations.idiomatic: On Boyou's mission, Yan had his Army Commander Zang Dun receive him instead.

sentences.zh: 議者以此貶之。

translations.literal: Discussants used this to demean him.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators used this to demean him.

sentences.zh: 使還，除驃騎將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: When the embassy returned he was appointed General of Rapid Cavalry and Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the embassy returned he was appointed General of Rapid Cavalry and inspector of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州貪惏，妻安豐王元延明女，專為聚斂，貨賄公行，潤及親戚。

translations.literal: In the province he was greedy and grasping. His wife was the daughter of Prince Yuan Yanming of Anfeng; she devoted herself to amassing wealth. Bribes were openly practiced, and profit extended to kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he was greedy and grasping. His wife was the daughter of Prince Yuan Yanming of Anfeng; she devoted herself to amassing wealth. Bribes were openly practiced and profit extended to their kin.

sentences.zh: 戶口逃散，邑落空虛。

translations.literal: Household registers fled and scattered; districts and towns were left empty and hollow.
translations.idiomatic: Households fled and districts were left empty.

sentences.zh: 乃誣良民，云欲反叛，籍其資財，盡以入己，誅其丈夫，婦女配沒。

translations.literal: He then falsely accused good commoners, saying they intended rebellion, registered their assets, took them all for himself, executed their husbands, and assigned the women to confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely accused good commoners of intending rebellion, seized their assets for himself, executed their husbands, and assigned the women to confiscation.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨苦，聲聞四方。

translations.literal: The people's resentment and suffering were heard in all four directions.
translations.idiomatic: The people's resentment was heard in all four directions.

sentences.zh: 為御史糾劾，死罪數十條，遇赦免，因以頓廢。

translations.literal: He was impeached by the censorate on dozens of capital offenses, encountered an amnesty and was spared, and thereby fell into sudden ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate impeached him on dozens of capital offenses. He was spared by an amnesty but fell into sudden ruin.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王作相，每誡厲朝士，常以伯猷及崔叔仁為諭。

translations.literal: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi served as Chancellor, he often admonished court gentlemen, regularly using Boyou and Cui Shuren as examples.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi served as Chancellor, he often admonished court gentlemen, regularly citing Boyou and Cui Shuren as cautionary examples.

sentences.zh: 武定七年，除太常卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuding he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuding (549) he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、中書監、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 伯猷弟仲衡，武定中，儀同開府中郎。

translations.literal: Boyou's younger brother Zhongheng, in the Wuding era, was Bureau Director of the Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Boyou's younger brother Zhongheng served as Bureau Director of the Office Equal to the Three Excellencies during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 仲衡弟輯之，解褐奉朝請，領侍御史，以軍功賜爵城臯男。

translations.literal: Zhongheng's younger brother Jizhi, upon leaving the russet, served as Court Gentleman for Attendance, concurrently as Attending Censor, and for military merit was granted the title Baron of Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongheng's younger brother Jizhi, upon entering service, served as Court Gentleman for Attendance and concurrent Attending Censor, and for military merit was ennobled as Baron of Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 稍遷黎陽太守。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 屬元顥入洛，令其舅范遵鎮守滑臺，與輯之隔岸相對。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; he ordered his maternal uncle Fan Zun to guard Huatai, facing Jizhi across the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he ordered his maternal uncle Fan Zun to guard Huatai, facing Jizhi across the river.

sentences.zh: 遵潛軍夜渡，規欲掩襲，輯之率厲城民，拒河擊之，遵遂遁走。

translations.literal: Zun secretly crossed the army by night, intending a surprise attack. Jizhi led and encouraged the city folk, repelled them at the river, and struck; Zun then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zun crossed by night intending a surprise attack. Jizhi rallied the townspeople, repelled them at the river, and Zun fled.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，除司州別駕。

translations.literal: The court commended him and appointed him Vice-Prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him and appointed him Vice-Prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋轉司空長史，遷鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and promoted to General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and promoted to General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，除征南將軍、東濟北太守，帶肥城戍主，男如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign he was appointed General Who Campaigns South and Administrator of Eastern Jibei, concurrently Garrison Commander of Feicheng, his baronage unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was appointed General Who Campaigns South and administrator of Eastern Jibei, concurrently Garrison Commander of Feicheng, retaining his baronage.

sentences.zh: 天平四年卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tianping (537), aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈都督北豫梁二州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、度支尚書、北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted command over all military affairs of the two provinces of Northern Yu and Liang, General of Rapid Cavalry, Minister of Revenue, and Inspector of Northern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted command over military affairs of Northern Yu and Liang provinces, General of Rapid Cavalry, Minister of Revenue, and inspector of Northern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 輯之弟懷孝，武定中，司徒諮議。

translations.literal: Jizhi's younger brother Huaixiao, in the Wuding era, was Advisory Staff Officer to the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's younger brother Huaixiao served as Advisory Staff Officer to the Minister of State during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 洞林子敬叔，[4]司州都官從事、滎陽邑中正，濮陽太守。

translations.literal: Donglin's son Jingshu [4], Attendant of the Capital Punishments Section of Sizhou, Rectifier of Xingyang district, Administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Donglin's son Jingshu [4] served as Attendant of the Capital Punishments Section of Sizhou, Rectifier of Xingyang district, and administrator of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 坐貪穢除名。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for greed and corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office for greed and corruption.

sentences.zh: 子籍，字承宗。

translations.literal: His son Ji, styled Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji, courtesy name Chengzong,

sentences.zh: 徐州平東府長史。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-East Headquarters of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: served as Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-East Headquarters of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 籍弟瓊，字祖珍，有強幹之稱。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Qiong, styled Zuzhen, had the reputation of strong capability.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Qiong, courtesy name Zuzhen, had a reputation for strong capability.

sentences.zh: 自太尉諮議為范陽太守，治頗有聲。

translations.literal: From Advisory Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant he became Administrator of Fanyang; his governance had considerable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: From Advisory Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant he became administrator of Fanyang, where his governance earned a good reputation.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，弟儼寵要，重贈安東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, because his younger brother Yan was favored and influential, he was again posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era, because his younger brother Yan was favored and influential, he was again posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 瓊兄弟雍睦，其諸娣姒亦咸相親愛，閨門之內有無相通，為時人所稱美。

translations.literal: The Qiong brothers were harmonious; their sisters-in-law also all loved one another, and within the inner quarters they shared what they had without distinction—praised by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiong brothers were harmonious, and their sisters-in-law also loved one another. Within the household they shared freely without distinction, which men of the time praised.

sentences.zh: 子道邕，歿關西。

translations.literal: His son Daoyong died in the lands west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoyong died in the lands west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 儼事在恩倖傳。

translations.literal: Yan's affairs are recorded in the Biographies of Favored Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's affairs are recorded in the Biographies of Favored Retainers.

sentences.zh: 敬叔弟士恭，燕郡太守。

translations.literal: Jingshu's younger brother Shigong was Administrator of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshu's younger brother Shigong was administrator of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，因儼之勢，除衞尉少卿，尋遷左將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, through Yan's influence, he was appointed Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies, then transferred to Left General and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era, through Yan's influence, he was appointed Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies, then transferred to Left General and inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮寇竊河北，州城淪陷，不獲之鎮。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Rong raided and stole through Hebei; the provincial city fell, and he could not take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ge Rong raided Hebei; the provincial city fell and he could not take up his post.

sentences.zh: 尋除征北將軍、金紫光祿大夫，又遷衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Campaigns North and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, then transferred to General of the Guards and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed General Who Campaigns North and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, then transferred to General of the Guards and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 永熙中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Yongxi era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Yongxi era.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎將軍、冀州刺史，重贈尚書左僕射，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General of Rapid Cavalry and Inspector of Jizhou, and again posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General of Rapid Cavalry and inspector of Jizhou, and again posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous name Zhen—"Upright."

sentences.zh: 長子子貞，司空掾。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zizhen was a clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zizhen was a clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 遷從事中郎、南兗州開府司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant, then Staff Officer of the Southern Yanzhou Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant, then Staff Officer of the Southern Yanzhou Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 子貞弟子湛，齊濟二州長史、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Zizhen's nephew Zhan served as Chief Clerk of Qi and Ji provinces and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen's nephew Zhan served as Chief Clerk of Qi and Ji provinces and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子湛弟昭伯，武定中，東平太守。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Zhaobo, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Zhaobo was administrator of Dongping during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 昭伯弟子嘉，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhaobo's nephew Jia died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaobo's nephew Jia died young.

sentences.zh: 子大護，武定中，司空戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Jia's son Dahu, in the Wuding era, was Household Staff Officer of the Minister of Works.
