translations.idiomatic: Jia's son Dahu served as Household Staff Officer of the Minister of Works during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 叔夜子伯夏，司徒諮議、東萊太守。

translations.literal: Shuye's son Boxia was Advisory Staff Officer to the Minister of State and Administrator of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye's son Boxia was Advisory Staff Officer to the Minister of State and administrator of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、太常少卿、青州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Champion General, Vice Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted Champion General, Vice Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, and inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子忠，字周子。

translations.literal: His son Zhong, styled Zhouzi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong, courtesy name Zhouzi,

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍、鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: Right Army General and General Who Guards the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: served as Right Army General and General Who Guards the Distance.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平東將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟豪，長水校尉、東平原太守。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hao was Commandant of the Chang River and Administrator of Eastern Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hao was Commandant of the Chang River and administrator of Eastern Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 伯夏弟謹，字仲恭。

translations.literal: Boxia's younger brother Jin, styled Zhonggong.
translations.idiomatic: Boxia's younger brother Jin, courtesy name Zhonggong,

sentences.zh: 琅邪太守。

translations.literal: Administrator of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: was administrator of Langye.

sentences.zh: 子嵩賓，歷尚書郎、員外常侍，稍遷至左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Songbin served as Master of Writing, Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment, and was gradually promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Songbin served as Master of Writing, Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment, and was gradually promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 連山，性嚴暴，撾撻僮僕，酷過人理。

translations.literal: Lianshan was severe and violent by nature, beating servants and slaves beyond human reason.
translations.idiomatic: Lianshan was severe and violent by nature, beating servants beyond all human reason.

sentences.zh: 父子一時為奴所害，斷首投馬槽下，乘馬北逝。

translations.literal: Father and son were at one time killed by slaves, their heads cut off and thrown under the horse trough; the killers rode north and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were killed by their slaves, their heads cut off and thrown under the horse trough. The killers rode north and fled.

sentences.zh: 其第二子思明，驍勇善騎射，披髮率村義，馳騎追之，及於河。

translations.literal: His second son Siming was brave and skilled in horse-archery. With hair unbound he led village volunteers in pursuit and caught them at the river.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Siming was brave and skilled in horse-archery. With hair unbound he led village volunteers in pursuit and caught them at the river.

sentences.zh: 奴乘馬投水，思明止將從不聽放矢，乃自射之，一發而中，落馬隨流，眾人擒執至家，臠而殺之。

translations.literal: The slave rode into the water; Siming stopped his followers from shooting and shot himself—one arrow struck home, the man fell from his horse and drifted with the current. The crowd seized him, brought him home, and cut him to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The slave rode into the water. Siming stopped his followers from shooting and shot himself—one arrow struck home. The man fell from his horse and drifted with the current. They seized him, brought him home, and cut him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 思明及弟思和，並以武功自効。

translations.literal: Siming and his younger brother Sihe both achieved merit through military skill.
translations.idiomatic: Siming and his younger brother Sihe both achieved merit through military skill.

sentences.zh: 思明至驍騎將軍、直閤將軍，坐弟思和同元禧逆徙邊。

translations.literal: Siming reached General of Rapid Cavalry and Direct Camp General; he was punished for his younger brother Sihe's involvement in Yuan Xi's rebellion and exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Siming rose to General of Rapid Cavalry and Direct Camp General. He was punished for his younger brother Sihe's involvement in Yuan Xi's rebellion and exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 會赦，卒於家。

translations.literal: He encountered an amnesty and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered an amnesty and died at home.

sentences.zh: 後贈冠軍將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Champion General and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously granted Champion General and inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子先護，少有武幹。

translations.literal: His son Xianhu from youth had martial capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianhu from youth had martial capacity.

sentences.zh: 解褐員外郎，轉通直郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the russet he served as Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment and was transferred to Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving the russet he served as Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment and was transferred to Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 莊帝之居藩也，先護深自結託。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was still in his princely residence, Xianhu deeply attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was still in his princely residence, Xianhu deeply attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱榮稱兵向洛，靈太后令先護與鄭季明等固守河梁，先護聞莊帝即位於河北，遂開門納榮。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang, Empress Dowager Ling ordered Xianhu with Zheng Jiming and others to hold the River Bridge firmly. Xianhu heard that Emperor Zhuang had been enthroned in Hebei and opened the gate to admit Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang, Empress Dowager Ling ordered Xianhu with Zheng Jiming and others to hold the River Bridge. Xianhu heard that Emperor Zhuang had been enthroned in Hebei and opened the gate to admit Rong.

sentences.zh: 以功封平昌縣開國侯，邑七百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchang district, with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchang district, with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉通常侍，[5]加鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant [5] and given the additional rank of General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant [5] and given the additional rank of General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 尋除前將軍、廣州刺史、假平南將軍、當州都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Forward General, Inspector of Guangzhou, acting General Who Pacifies the South, and Regional Commander of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Forward General, inspector of Guangzhou, acting General Who Pacifies the South, and regional commander of the province.

sentences.zh: 時妖賊劉舉於濮陽起逆，詔先護以本官為東道都督討舉平之。

translations.literal: At that time the sorcerer-rebel Liu Ju rose in Puyang. An edict ordered Xianhu, in his former office, to serve as Eastern Route Commander to attack and pacify Ju.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sorcerer-rebel Liu Ju rose in Puyang. An edict ordered Xianhu, in his former office, to serve as Eastern Route Commander to attack and pacify Ju.

sentences.zh: 還鎮。

translations.literal: He returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his garrison.

sentences.zh: 後元顥入洛，莊帝北巡，先護據州起義兵，不受顥命。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; Emperor Zhuang toured the north, and Xianhu raised righteous troops in the province, refusing Hao's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; Emperor Zhuang toured the north, and Xianhu raised righteous troops in the province, refusing Hao's orders.

sentences.zh: 顥遣尚書令、臨淮王彧率眾討之，[6]先護出城拒戰。

translations.literal: Hao sent the Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Huai'nan Yu, to lead troops against him. [6] Xianhu went out of the city to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hao sent the Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince Yu of Huai'nan, to lead troops against him. [6] Xianhu went out of the city to give battle.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還京，嘉其誠節，除使持節、散騎常侍、都督襄廣二州諸軍事、鎮南將軍，刺史如故，進爵郡公，增邑一千三百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the capital, he commended Xianhu's loyalty and appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, Commander of all military affairs of the two provinces of Xiang and Guang, General Who Guards the South, inspector unchanged, promoted to Duke of the commandery with fief increased by 1,300 households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the capital, he commended Xianhu's loyalty and appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, commander of military affairs of Xiang and Guang provinces, General Who Guards the South, inspector unchanged, promoted to Duke of the commandery with fief increased by 1,300 households.

sentences.zh: 尋轉征西將軍、東雍州刺史、假車騎將軍、當州都督，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Campaigns West, Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou, acting General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Regional Commander of the province, Attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to General Who Campaigns West, inspector of Eastern Yongzhou, acting General of the Chariots and Cavalry, regional commander of the province, Attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 未之任，又轉都督二豫東雍三州諸軍事、征東將軍、豫州刺史，餘官如故。

translations.literal: Before taking up the post he was again transferred to Commander of all military affairs of the three provinces of Second Yu, Eastern Yong, and Inspector of Yuzhou, other offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking up the post he was again transferred to commander of military affairs of Second Yu, Eastern Yong, and Yuzhou, other offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又兼尚書右僕射、二豫郢潁四州行臺。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Headquarters of the four provinces of Second Yu, Ying, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Headquarters of Second Yu, Ying, and Ying provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋除車騎將軍、左衞將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱榮死，徐州刺史尒朱仲遠擁兵向洛，前至東郡。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Erzhu Zhongyuan of Xuzhou gathered troops toward Luoyang and advanced to Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Erzhu Zhongyuan of Xuzhou gathered troops toward Luoyang and advanced to Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 諸軍出討，不能制之。

translations.literal: The armies went out to attack but could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: The armies went out to attack but could not control him.

sentences.zh: 乃詔先護以本官假驃騎將軍、大都督，領所部與行臺楊昱同討之。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Xianhu, in his former office with acting rank as General of Rapid Cavalry and Supreme Commander, to lead his command together with Mobile Headquarters Yang Yu to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Xianhu, in his former office with acting rank as General of Rapid Cavalry and Supreme Commander, to lead his command with Mobile Headquarters Yang Yu to attack him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝又遣都督賀拔勝討仲遠，勝於陳降賊，戰士離心。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang also sent Regional Commander Heba Sheng to attack Zhongyuan. Sheng surrendered to the enemy at Chen; the warriors lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang also sent Regional Commander Heba Sheng to attack Zhongyuan. Sheng surrendered to the enemy at Chen and the warriors lost heart.

sentences.zh: 尋聞京師不守，先護部眾逃散，遂竄伏於南境。

translations.literal: Soon they heard the capital was lost; Xianhu's troops scattered and fled, and he hid in the southern marches.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they heard the capital was lost. Xianhu's troops scattered and he hid in the southern marches.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，仲遠遣人招誘之，既出而害焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Former Emperor's reign, Zhongyuan sent men to entice him; once he came out he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Deposed Former Emperor's reign, Zhongyuan sent men to entice him; once he came out he was killed.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，贈持節、都督青齊濟兗四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、青州刺史，開國如故。

translations.literal: In Emperor Chu's time he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of the four provinces of Qing, Qi, Ji, and Yan, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Qingzhou, his marquisate unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Chu's time he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs of Qing, Qi, Ji, and Yan provinces, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, inspector of Qingzhou, his marquisate unchanged.

sentences.zh: 思和，歷太尉中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Sihe served as Middle Army Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Sihe served as Middle Army Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 同元禧之逆，伏法。

translations.literal: Together with Yuan Xi's rebellion he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yuan Xi's rebellion he was executed.

sentences.zh: 子康業，通直郎。

translations.literal: His son Kangye was Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kangye was Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，坐事賜死。

translations.literal: In Emperor Chu's time he was sentenced to death for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Chu's time he was sentenced to death for an offense.

sentences.zh: 子彬，武定末，齊王相國中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Bin, at the end of Wuding, was Middle Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Qi, Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin, at the end of Wuding, was Middle Army Staff Officer to the Prince of Qi, Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 思和弟季長，太學博士。

translations.literal: Sihe's younger brother Jichang was Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Sihe's younger brother Jichang was Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子喬，歷司州治中、驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Qiao served as Chief Clerk of Sizhou, General of Rapid Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiao served as Chief Clerk of Sizhou, General of Rapid Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 羲叔父簡，簡孫尚，壯健有將略。

translations.literal: Xi's paternal uncle Jian; Jian's grandson Shang was robust and had military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's paternal uncle Jian; Jian's grandson Shang was robust and had military strategy.

sentences.zh: 屢為統軍，東西征討，以軍功賜爵汝陽男。

translations.literal: Repeatedly serving as supreme commander, campaigning east and west, he was granted the title Baron of Ruyang for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly serving as supreme commander on eastern and western campaigns, he was ennobled as Baron of Ruyang for military merit.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書郎、步兵校尉、驍騎將軍，遷輔國將軍、太尉司馬。

translations.literal: He served as Master of Writing, Commandant of Footsoldiers, General of Rapid Cavalry, and was transferred to General Who Assists the State and Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Master of Writing, Commandant of Footsoldiers, General of Rapid Cavalry, and was transferred to General Who Assists the State and Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 出為濟州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Jizhou, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of Jizhou, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 為政寬簡，百姓安之。

translations.literal: His government was generous and simple; the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His government was generous and simple; the people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted his former general's rank, Inspector of Yuzhou, with the posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted his former general's rank and inspector of Yuzhou, with the posthumous name Hui—"Kind."

sentences.zh: 子貴賓，襲。

translations.literal: His son Guibin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guibin inherited.

sentences.zh: 解褐北海王國常侍。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the russet he served as Regular Attendant of the Prince of Beihai's kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving the russet he served as Regular Attendant of the Prince of Beihai's kingdom.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎，稍遷尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment; he was gradually promoted to Master of the Gold Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment; he was gradually promoted to Master of the Gold Section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以公坐免官。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for a public offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office for a public offense.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼太尉屬。

translations.literal: After a long time he concurrently served as Attendant of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he concurrently served as Attendant of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子景裕，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingyu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingyu inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定末，儀同開府行參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Mobile Staff Officer of the Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was Mobile Staff Officer of the Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 貴賓弟次珍，卒於員外常侍。

translations.literal: Guibin's younger brother Cizhen died while serving as Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Guibin's younger brother Cizhen died while serving as Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment.

sentences.zh: 贈安東將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貴賓異母弟大倪、小倪。

translations.literal: Guibin's younger half-brothers Dani and Xiaoni.
translations.idiomatic: Guibin's younger half-brothers Dani and Xiaoni

sentences.zh: 皆粗險薄行，好為劫盜，侵暴鄉里，百姓毒患之。

translations.literal: Both were coarse, dangerous, and of shallow conduct, fond of robbery and plunder, invading and oppressing their home districts. The people suffered bitterly from them.
translations.idiomatic: were both coarse, dangerous, and of shallow conduct, fond of robbery and plunder, invading their home districts. The people suffered bitterly from them.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，並為尒朱仲遠所殺。

translations.literal: In the Putai era both were killed by Erzhu Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Putai era both were killed by Erzhu Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 尚從父兄雲，字道漢。

translations.idiomatic: Shang's elder cousin's son Yun, courtesy name Daohan,

translations.idiomatic: He served in Yanmen and Puyang, greedy and corrupt beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，納賄劉騰，得為龍驤將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: In Emperor Suzong's time he bribed Liu Teng and was made General of the Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Suzong's time he bribed Liu Teng and was made General of the Dragon Cavalry and inspector of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐選舉受財，為御史所糾，因暴病卒。

translations.literal: He was impeached by the censorate for taking bribes in selections and died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate impeached him for taking bribes in selections and he died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 雲從父兄子敬賓，自祕書郎稍遷輔國將軍、中散大夫、魏郡太守、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.idiomatic: Yun's elder cousin's son Jingbin rose from Secretary of the Palace Library to General Who Assists the State, Palace Attendant, administrator of Wei Commandery, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 子士淵，司空行參軍。

translations.literal: His son Shiyuan was Mobile Staff Officer of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiyuan was Mobile Staff Officer of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 羲從父兄德玄。

translations.literal: Xi's elder cousin's son Dexuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's elder cousin's son Dexuan.

sentences.zh: 顯祖初，自淮南內附，拜滎陽太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xianzu's reign he submitted from within Huainan and was appointed Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xianzu's reign he submitted from Huainan and was appointed administrator of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 子子考，太和中，復為滎陽太守。

translations.literal: His son Zikao, in the Taihe era, again served as Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zikao again served as administrator of Xingyang in the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、豫州刺史、開封侯，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Champion General, Inspector of Yuzhou, Marquis of Kaifeng, with the posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted Champion General, inspector of Yuzhou, Marquis of Kaifeng, with the posthumous name Hui—"Kind."

sentences.zh: 子洪建，太尉祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Hongjian was Libationer of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjian was Libationer of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 同元禧之逆，與弟祖育同伏法。

translations.literal: Together with Yuan Xi's rebellion he and his younger brother Zuyu were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yuan Xi's rebellion he and his younger brother Zuyu were both executed.

sentences.zh: 永安中，特追贈平東將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was specially posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was specially posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 子士機，性識不周，多有短失。

translations.literal: His son Shiji was limited in understanding and had many faults.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiji was limited in understanding and had many faults.

sentences.zh: 歷散騎侍郎、司空從事中郎、中書郎。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, Attendant of the Minister of Works, and Master of Writing of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, Attendant of the Minister of Works, and Master of Writing of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子道蔭，武定末，開府行參軍。

translations.literal: His son Daoyin, at the end of Wuding, was Mobile Staff Officer of the Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoyin served as Mobile Staff Officer of the Office Equal to the Three Excellencies at the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 祖育，太尉祭酒。

translations.literal: Zuyu, Libationer of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu, Libationer of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 亦特贈平東將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also specially posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also specially posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖育弟仲明，奉朝請，稍遷太尉屬。

translations.literal: Zuyu's younger brother Zhongming was Court Gentleman for Attendance and was gradually promoted to Attendant of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu's younger brother Zhongming was Court Gentleman for Attendance and was gradually promoted to Attendant of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 以公強當世，為從弟儼所昵，除滎陽太守。

translations.literal: Because of his public power in the age he was favored by his cousin Yan and was appointed Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his public power in the age he was favored by his cousin Yan and was appointed administrator of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 儼慮世難，欲以東道託之。

translations.literal: Yan, fearing the troubles of the age, wished to entrust the eastern route to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, fearing the troubles of the age, wished to entrust the eastern route to him.

sentences.zh: 建義初，仲明弟季明遇害河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Zhongming's younger brother Jiming was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi, Zhongming's younger brother Jiming was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 儼後歸之，欲與起兵，尋為城民所殺。

translations.literal: Yan later returned and wished to raise troops with him, but was soon killed by the city folk.
translations.idiomatic: Yan later returned and wished to raise troops with him, but was soon killed by the city folk.

sentences.zh: 仲明兄洪健，李沖女壻。

translations.literal: Zhongming's elder brother Hongjian was son-in-law to Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongming's elder brother Hongjian was son-in-law to Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 建義初，莊帝以仲明舅氏之親，其弟與謀扶戴，仲明之死也，且有奉國之意，乃追封安平縣開國侯、邑七百戶，贈侍中、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、尚書左僕射、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Emperor Zhuang, because of Zhongming's kinship as maternal uncle, and because his younger brother had plotted to support and enthrone him, and because Zhongming's death also had the intent of serving the state, posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Anping district with a fief of seven hundred households and granted Attendant, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi, Emperor Zhuang, because of Zhongming's kinship as maternal uncle and because his death had shown intent to serve the state, posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Anping district with seven hundred households and granted Attendant, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 長子道門，仲明初謀起義，令道門說大都督李叔仁於大梁。

translations.literal: His eldest son Daomen—when Zhongming first plotted the uprising he sent Daomen to persuade the Supreme Commander Li Shuren at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Daomen—when Zhongming first plotted the uprising he sent Daomen to persuade Supreme Commander Li Shuren at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 叔仁始欲同舉，後聞莊帝已立，叔仁子拔江乃斬道門。

translations.literal: Shuren at first wished to join the rising, but later heard Emperor Zhuang had been enthroned; Shuren's son Baojiang then beheaded Daomen.
translations.idiomatic: Shuren at first wished to join, but later heard Emperor Zhuang had been enthroned; Shuren's son Baojiang then beheaded Daomen.

sentences.zh: 建義中，特贈立節將軍、瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Jianyi era he was specially posthumously granted General Who Establishes Integrity and Inspector of Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianyi era he was specially posthumously granted General Who Establishes Integrity and inspector of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 道門弟孝邕，襲。

translations.literal: Daomen's younger brother Xiaoyong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Daomen's younger brother Xiaoyong inherited.

sentences.zh: 天保初，爵隨例降。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao the title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao the title was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 仲明弟季亮，司徒城局參軍、員外常侍。

translations.literal: Zhongming's younger brother Jiliang was Staff Officer of the City Bureau of the Minister of State and Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongming's younger brother Jiliang was Staff Officer of the City Bureau of the Minister of State and Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈散騎常侍、撫軍將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the Army, and inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 季亮弟季明，釋褐太學博士。

translations.literal: Jiliang's younger brother Jiming, upon leaving the russet, was Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Jiliang's younger brother Jiming, upon leaving the russet, was Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 正光中，譙郡太守，帶渦陽戍主。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he was Administrator of Qiao Commandery, concurrently Garrison Commander of Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era he was administrator of Qiao Commandery, concurrently Garrison Commander of Woyang.

sentences.zh: 頻為蕭衍遣將攻圍，兵糧寡少，外援不接，季明孤城自守，卒得保全。

translations.literal: Repeatedly attacked and besieged by generals sent by Xiao Yan, with few troops and grain and no external relief, Jiming held the isolated city and in the end preserved it.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly attacked and besieged by generals sent by Xiao Yan, with few troops and grain and no relief, Jiming held the isolated city and preserved it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，封安德縣開國伯，邑七百戶。

translations.literal: The court commended him and enfeoffed him as Baron of Ande district with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him and enfeoffed him as Baron of Ande district with seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 累遷平東將軍、光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Vice Director of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Vice Director of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 武泰中，潛通尒朱榮，謀奉莊帝。

translations.literal: In the Wutai era he secretly communicated with Erzhu Rong, plotting to enthrone Emperor Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wutai era he secretly communicated with Erzhu Rong, plotting to enthrone Emperor Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 及在河陽，遂為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: When at Heyang he was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyang he was killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 事寧，追封南潁川郡開國公，食邑千五百戶，贈驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、司空公、定州刺史。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Southern Yingchuan commandery with a fief of 1,500 households and granted Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Southern Yingchuan commandery with 1,500 households and granted Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子昌，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定末，司徒城局參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Staff Officer of the City Bureau of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was Staff Officer of the City Bureau of the Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 天保初，爵隨例降。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao the title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao the title was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 崔辯，字神通，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Bian, styled Shentong, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bian, courtesy name Shentong, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 學涉經史，風儀整峻。

translations.literal: He studied the classics and histories; his bearing was orderly and stern.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics and histories; his bearing was orderly and stern.

sentences.zh: 顯祖徵拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu summoned and appointed him Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu summoned and appointed him Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎、平遠將軍、武邑太守。

translations.literal: Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the Distance, Administrator of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the Distance, administrator of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 政事之餘，專以勸學為務。

translations.literal: In the spare time from government affairs he devoted himself solely to encouraging learning.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from government affairs he devoted himself solely to encouraging learning.

sentences.zh: 年六十二，卒。

translations.literal: At age sixty-two he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈安南將軍、定州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the South and inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous name Gong—"Reverent."

sentences.zh: 長子景儁，梗正有高風，好古博涉。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jingjun was upright with lofty character and loved antiquity with broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jingjun was upright with lofty character and loved antiquity with broad learning.

sentences.zh: 以經明行修，徵拜中書博士。

translations.literal: For clarity in the classics and cultivation in conduct he was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For clarity in the classics and cultivation in conduct he was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歷侍御史、主文中散。

translations.literal: He served as Attending Censor and Chief Palace Attendant for Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attending Censor and Chief Palace Attendant for Drafting.

sentences.zh: 受敕接蕭頤使蕭琛、范雲，高祖賜名為逸。

translations.literal: He received orders to receive the envoys of Xiao Yan, Xiao Chen and Fan Yun; Emperor Gaozu granted him the name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He received orders to receive the envoys of Xiao Yan, Xiao Chen and Fan Yun; Emperor Gaozu granted him the name Yi.

sentences.zh: 後為員外散騎侍郎，與著作郎韓興宗參定朝儀。

translations.literal: Later he was Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment and with the Authoring Gentleman Han Xingzong helped fix court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment and with Authoring Gentleman Han Xingzong helped fix court ritual.

sentences.zh: 雅為高祖所知重，遷國子博士，每有公事，逸常被詔獨進。

translations.literal: He was well known and valued by Emperor Gaozu; he was transferred to Erudite of the National University. Whenever there was public business Yi was often ordered to enter alone.
translations.idiomatic: He was well known and valued by Emperor Gaozu; he was transferred to Erudite of the National University. Whenever there was public business Yi was often ordered to enter alone.

sentences.zh: 博士特命，自逸始。

translations.literal: Special orders to erudites began with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Special orders to erudites began with Yi.

sentences.zh: 轉通直散騎常侍、廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Direct Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and Vice Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒，朝廷悼惜之，贈以本官。

translations.literal: When he died the court mourned and regretted him, posthumously granting his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the court mourned him and posthumously granted his former office.

sentences.zh: 子巨倫，字孝宗。

translations.literal: His son Julun, styled Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Julun, courtesy name Xiaozong,

sentences.zh: 幼孤，及長，歷涉經史，有文學武藝。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, when grown he ranged through the classics and histories and had both literary learning and martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, when grown he ranged through the classics and histories and had both literary learning and martial skill.

sentences.zh: 以世宗挽郎，除冀州鎮北府墨曹參軍、太尉記室參軍。

translations.literal: As a mourning officer for Emperor Shizong he was appointed Ink Bureau Staff Officer of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters of Jizhou and Recording Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: As a mourning officer for Emperor Shizong he was appointed Ink Bureau Staff Officer of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters of Jizhou and Recording Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 叔楷為殷州，巨倫仍為長史、北道別將。

translations.literal: His uncle Kai served as inspector of Yinzhou; Julun remained as Chief Clerk and Northern Route Deputy Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Kai served as inspector of Yinzhou; Julun remained as Chief Clerk and Northern Route Deputy Commander.

sentences.zh: 在州陷賊，斂恤亡存，為賊所義。

translations.literal: In the province they fell to bandits; he gathered and comforted the dead and living and was regarded with righteousness by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the province they fell to bandits; he gathered and comforted the dead and living and was regarded with righteousness by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 葛榮聞其才名，欲用為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Ge Rong heard his talent and reputation and wished to use him as Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong heard his talent and wished to use him as Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 巨倫心惡之。

translations.literal: Julun hated this in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Julun hated this in his heart.

sentences.zh: 至五月五日，會集官僚，令巨倫賦詩，巨倫乃曰：「五月五日時，天氣已大熱。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month they gathered officials and ordered Julun to compose a poem. Julun said: "On the fifth day of the fifth month the weather is already very hot."
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month they gathered officials and ordered Julun to compose a poem. Julun said, "On the fifth day of the fifth month the weather is already very hot."

sentences.zh: 狗便呀欲死，牛復吐出舌。

translations.literal: Dogs open their jaws as if to die; oxen stick out their tongues again."
translations.idiomatic: Dogs open their jaws as if to die; oxen stick out their tongues again."

sentences.zh: 」以此自晦，獲免。

translations.literal: By this he obscured himself and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: By this he obscured himself and was spared.

sentences.zh: 未幾，潛結死士數人，夜中南走，逢賊遊騎數百，俱恐不濟。

translations.literal: Before long he secretly joined several men willing to die and fled south by night, encountering several hundred bandit patrol horsemen; all feared they would not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he secretly joined several men willing to die and fled south by night, encountering several hundred bandit patrol horsemen; all feared they would not succeed.

sentences.zh: 巨倫曰：「寧南死一寸，豈北生一尺也！

translations.literal: Julun said: "Better to die an inch in the south than live a foot in the north!"
translations.idiomatic: Julun said, "Better to die an inch in the south than live a foot in the north!"

sentences.zh: 」便欺賊曰：「吾受敕而行。

translations.literal: He then deceived the bandits, saying: "I am traveling on imperial orders."
translations.idiomatic: He then deceived the bandits, saying, "I am traveling on imperial orders."

sentences.zh: 」賊不信，共爇火觀敕。

translations.literal: The bandits did not believe him and together lit a fire to view the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits did not believe him and together lit a fire to view the edict.

sentences.zh: 火未然，巨倫手刃賊帥，餘人因與奮擊，殺傷數十人，賊乃四潰，得馬數匹而去。

translations.literal: Before the fire caught, Julun slew the bandit chief with his own hand; the rest joined in striking fiercely, killing and wounding several tens. The bandits then scattered in four directions, and they obtained several horses and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before the fire caught, Julun slew the bandit chief with his own hand; the rest joined in striking fiercely, killing and wounding dozens. The bandits scattered and they obtained several horses and fled.

sentences.zh: 夜陰失道，惟看佛塔戶而行。

translations.literal: In the dark night they lost the road and could only proceed by watching the doors of pagodas.
translations.idiomatic: In the dark night they lost the road and could only proceed by watching the doors of pagodas.

sentences.zh: 到洛，朝廷嘉之，授持節、別將北討。

translations.literal: When they reached Luoyang the court commended him and appointed him Bearer of the Staff and Deputy Commander of the Northern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Luoyang the court commended him and appointed him Bearer of the Staff and Deputy Commander of the Northern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 初，楷喪之始，巨倫收殯倉卒，事不周固，至是遂偷路改殯，并竊家口以歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the beginning of Kai's mourning, Julun had gathered the burial in haste and matters were not thorough. Now he secretly changed the route of the coffin and also stole household members to return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the beginning of Kai's mourning, Julun had gathered the burial in haste and matters were not thorough. Now he secretly changed the route of the coffin and also stole household members to return.

sentences.zh: 尋授國子博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，假節、中堅將軍、東濮陽太守，假征虜將軍、別將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned he was given acting staff, General of the Firm Center, Administrator of Eastern Puyang, acting General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Deputy Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned he was given acting staff, General of the Firm Center, administrator of Eastern Puyang, acting General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Deputy Commander.

sentences.zh: 時河北紛梗，人士避賊，多住郡界，歲儉飢乏，巨倫傾資贍恤，務相全濟，時類高之。

translations.literal: At that time Hebei was in turmoil and gentlemen fleeing bandits mostly stayed within the commandery borders. In years of famine and hunger Julun poured out his resources to support and save them, striving to preserve them all—men of the time esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hebei was in turmoil and gentlemen fleeing bandits mostly stayed within the commandery. In years of famine Julun poured out his resources to support them, striving to preserve them all—men of the time esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，據郡不從。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he held the commandery and did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he held the commandery and did not submit.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，行西兗州事，封漁陽縣開國男，邑二百戶，尋除光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace he acted for Western Yanzhou, was enfeoffed as Baron of Yuyang district with a fief of two hundred households, and soon was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace he acted for Western Yanzhou, was enfeoffed as Baron of Yuyang district with two hundred households, and soon was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 三年卒，時年四十四。

translations.literal: He died in the third year, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year, aged forty-four.

sentences.zh: 子武，襲。

translations.literal: His son Wu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wu inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定中，懷州衞軍府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was Recording Staff Officer of the Guards Army Headquarters of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was Recording Staff Officer of the Guards Army Headquarters of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate the title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate the title was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 初，巨倫有姊，明惠有才行，因患眇一目，內外親類莫有求者，其家議欲下嫁之。

translations.literal: Earlier Julun had an elder sister, bright and capable, who because of illness had one eye blinded. No one among kin inside or outside sought her in marriage, and the family discussed marrying her down.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Julun had an elder sister, bright and capable, who because of illness had one eye blinded. No kin sought her in marriage, and the family discussed marrying her beneath their station.

sentences.zh: 巨倫姑趙國李叔胤之妻，高明慈篤，聞而悲感曰：「吾兄盛德，不幸早世，豈令此女屈事卑族！

translations.literal: Julun's aunt, wife of Li Shuyin of Zhao, was lofty, bright, kind, and sincere. Hearing this she was moved to grief and said: "My brother's great virtue—unfortunate to die early. How can I let this girl submit to a low clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Julun's aunt, wife of Li Shuyin of Zhao, was lofty, bright, kind, and sincere. Hearing this she was moved to grief and said, "My brother's great virtue—unfortunate to die early. How can I let this girl submit to a low clan!"

sentences.zh: 」乃為子翼納之，時人歎其義。

translations.literal: She then took her as wife for her son Yi. Men of the time praised her righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: She then took her as wife for her son Yi. Men of the time praised her righteousness.

sentences.zh: 崔氏與翼書詩數十首，辭理可觀。

translations.literal: The Cui clan and Yi exchanged several tens of poems; the reasoning and style were admirable.
translations.idiomatic: The Cui clan and Yi exchanged several tens of poems; the reasoning and style were admirable.

sentences.zh: 逸弟模，字叔軌。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Mo, styled Shugui.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Mo, courtesy name Shugui,

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，圍亦如之。

translations.literal: His height was eight chi and his girth was the same.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall and his girth matched his height.

sentences.zh: 出後其叔。

translations.literal: He was adopted out to his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted out to his uncle.

sentences.zh: 雅有志度。

translations.literal: By nature he had lofty ambition and measure.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he had lofty ambition and measure.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請，歷太尉祭酒、尚書金部郎中、太尉主簿，轉中郎，遷太子家令。

translations.literal: He began his career as Court Gentleman for Attendance, served as Libationer of the Grand Commandant, Master of the Gold Section, Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant, was transferred to Attendant, and promoted to Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Court Gentleman for Attendance, served as Libationer of the Grand Commandant, Master of the Gold Section, Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant, was transferred to Attendant, and promoted to Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 以公事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for a public offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for a public offense.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，詔復本資，除冠軍將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era an edict restored his former salary and he was appointed Champion General and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengui era an edict restored his former salary and he was appointed Champion General and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出除魯陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out and was appointed Administrator of Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，襄陽民密求款附，詔模為別將，隸淮南王世遵，率眾赴之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang the people of Xiangyang secretly sought to submit. An edict made Mo Deputy Commander under Prince Shizun of Huainan, who led troops to go there.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang the people of Xiangyang secretly sought to submit. An edict made Mo Deputy Commander under Prince Shizun of Huainan, who led troops to go there.

sentences.zh: 事覺，模焚襄陽邑郭而還。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Mo burned the outer districts of Xiangyang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, Mo burned the outer districts of Xiangyang and returned.

sentences.zh: 坐不克，免官。

translations.literal: He was punished for failure to overcome the enemy and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for failure and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤討關隴，引模為西征別將，屢有戰功，除持節、光祿大夫、都督別道諸軍事，加安東將軍。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned against Guan and Long, he recruited Mo as Western Campaign Deputy Commander. He repeatedly had military achievements and was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Commander of all military affairs of the separate route, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned against Guan and Long, he recruited Mo as Western Campaign Deputy Commander. He won repeated victories and was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, commander of the separate route's military affairs, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 万俟醜奴遣將郝虎南侵，模攻破其營，擒虎。

translations.literal: Chounu of Wanqi sent his general Hao Hu south to invade; Mo broke his camp and captured Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu of Wanqi sent his general Hao Hu south to invade; Mo broke his camp and captured Hu.

sentences.zh: 以功封槐里縣開國伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Huaili district with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Huaili district with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 於時將督敗歿者多，模挫敵持重，號為名將。

translations.literal: At that time many supervising generals were defeated and killed; Mo checked the enemy and held his ground and was called a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many supervising generals were defeated and killed; Mo checked the enemy, held his ground, and was called a famous general.

sentences.zh: 後假征東將軍、行岐州事。

translations.literal: Later he was given acting rank as General Who Campaigns East and acted for Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was given acting rank as General Who Campaigns East and acted for Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擊賊入深，沒於陳。

translations.literal: Before long he attacked bandits and went deep; he perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he attacked bandits and went too deep; he perished in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the Army and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，追錄前勳，又贈都督定相冀三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、相州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era his former achievements were recorded posthumously again, and he was again granted command over all military affairs of the three provinces of Ding, Xiang, and Ji, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era his former achievements were recorded again, and he was again granted command over military affairs of Ding, Xiang, and Ji provinces, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子士護。

translations.literal: His son Shihu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shihu.

sentences.zh: 模弟楷，字季則。

translations.literal: Mo's younger brother Kai, styled Jize.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's younger brother Kai, courtesy name Jize,

sentences.zh: 美風望，性剛梗，有當世幹具。

translations.literal: He had fine bearing and presence; by nature he was firm and upright and had capacity for the age.
translations.idiomatic: He had fine bearing and presence; by nature he was firm and upright and had capacity for his age.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請，員外散騎侍郎、廣平王懷文學。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the russet he served as Court Gentleman for Attendance, Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment, and Literary Scholar to Prince Huai of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving the russet he served as Court Gentleman for Attendance, Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment, and Literary Scholar to Prince Huai of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 正始中，以王國官非其人，多被刑戮，惟楷與楊昱以數諫獲免。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, because princely household officials were not the right men, many were punished and killed; only Kai and Yang Yu were spared through repeated remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era, because princely household officials were unsuitable, many were punished and killed; only Kai and Yang Yu were spared through repeated remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左主客郎中、伏波將軍、太子中舍人、左中郎將。

translations.literal: Later he served as Director of the Left Guest Section of the Masters of Writing, General Who Subdues the Waves, Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, and Left Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Director of the Left Guest Section of the Masters of Writing, General Who Subdues the Waves, Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, and Left Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以黨附高肇，為中尉所劾，事在高聰傳。

translations.literal: For attaching himself to Gao Zhao he was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief; the affair is in the biography of Gao Cong.
translations.idiomatic: For attaching himself to Gao Zhao he was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief; the affair is in the biography of Gao Cong.

sentences.zh: 楷性嚴烈，能摧挫豪強，故時人語曰：「莫𢖇

translations.literal: Kai's nature was stern and fierce; he could break the power of the mighty. Thus people of the time said: "Do not haggle-buy
translations.idiomatic: Kai's nature was stern and fierce; he could break the power of the mighty. Thus people of the time said, "Do not haggle-buy—

translations.idiomatic: 〈du mai fan〉
